name: Contest Practice
description: Solve timed algorithm problems and learn to pick your battles in a contest.

lessonObjectives.l1-reading-statements: Pull the input limits out of a statement and say what they imply.
lessonObjectives.l2-limits-to-complexity: Choose an algorithm from the constraints before writing code.
lessonObjectives.l3-fast-io: Read and write large inputs quickly in Python and C++.
lessonObjectives.l4-stress-testing: Stress test a solution against a brute force on random cases.
lessonObjectives.l5-modulo: Compute with modular arithmetic, including modular inverses.
lessonObjectives.l6-gcd-and-primes: Use Euclid’s algorithm and a sieve.
lessonObjectives.l7-counting-mod: Compute binomial coefficients modulo a prime with factorial tables.
lessonObjectives.l8-invariants: Solve a problem by finding a quantity that never changes.
lessonObjectives.l9-constructive: Solve a constructive problem by building the output directly.
lessonObjectives.l10-greedy-proofs: Prove a greedy choice with an exchange argument.
lessonObjectives.l12-difference-arrays: Apply many range updates at once with a difference array.
lessonObjectives.l13-virtual-contest: Sit a timed virtual contest and log where the time went.
lessonObjectives.l14-which-first: Choose the order of problems by points and difficulty.
lessonObjectives.l15-debugging-under-time: Find a bug quickly with small hand-made cases.
lessonObjectives.l16-upsolving: Learn from the problems you could not solve in time.
